pipeline_name: Badra Oil Field–Wassit PS Gas Pipeline

validity.recommendation: Keep the row (real, correctly classified as gas transmission). Replace the two GEM citations (an OPC gov page now behind a JS security gateway, and a Facebook 'pigging' post that is about the whole 1065 km dry-gas network, not this line) with the independent OGJ / NS Energy sources; add commissioning date Dec 6, 2017.
validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE: CONFIRMED and well-documented. This is the ~100 km dry-gas pipeline that carries processed dry gas from the Gazprom Neft Badra field gas treatment plant (GTP, commissioned 6 Dec 2017, ~1.6 bcm/yr) to the Az-Zubaidiya (Al-Zubaidiya) power station in Wasit province. Independent confirmation: Oil & Gas Journal ('processes dry feed gas from Badra field, that will be shipped via a 100-km pipeline to the Az-Zubaidiya power station') and NS Energy ('Processed dry feed gas from the gas treatment plant is supplied through a 100km pipeline, mainly to meet the needs of the Az-Zubaidiya power station'). Offshore-technology corroborates the Badra field / Wasit / gas context. WHAT THE SHEET'S OWN SOURCES SHOW: the two cited refs do NOT independently support the specifics. (1) opc.oil.gov.iq/?article=198 now 307-redirects to a JavaScript security-verification gateway ('Processing your request...') that serves no article text — url_verifier FAILs it for every value token (status, 106.5, 18), so it is not machine-verifiable and cannot corroborate length/diameter. (2) The PipelinesIQ Facebook post is captioned 'بمسافة 1065 km ... انجاز اعمال القشط على انبوب الغاز الجاف' (pigging/scraping works over 1065 km of dry-gas pipe) — that 1065 km is the OPC dry-gas NETWORK total, NOT this line; it is not a length source for P7471 and the near-coincidence with 106.5 is a coincidence, not corroboration. CLASSIFICATION: CONFIRMED gas transmission trunk (processed dry gas, field GTP → power station, ~100 km). Not an oil/NGL line — it is absent from the GulfPub Iraq oil roster; the separate 'Badra-PS-2 Oil Pipeline' on gem.wiki is a distinct crude line. DUPLICATE: none. Roster neighbor P4067 (Al-Ahdab–Al-Zubaydia, 73 km / 16") feeds the SAME Az-Zubaidiya power station but from a DIFFERENT source field (Al-Ahdab / CNPC), so it is a parallel feeder, not a double-count of this Badra line. ATTRIBUTION: Operator 'Oil Pipelines Co' (OPC) / Owner 'Iraq Ministry of Oil' is plausible for a national dry-gas trunk and consistent with the PipelinesIQ/OPC social posts; province Wassit is correct (both endpoints are in Wasit). Gazprom Neft built the GTP but the trunk to the power station is Iraqi state infrastructure. SPEC: see spec validity object.

validity.recommendation: Treat LengthKnown=106.5 km as acceptable (independent sources round to '100 km'; the routed distance Badra field→Zubaidiya PS is ~95 km straight-line, so ~100–106.5 km routed is consistent). Diameter=18 in is UNVERIFIED by any independent source — flag low-confidence, keep but do not treat as corroborated. Capacity is blank and cannot be responsibly filled (the 1.6 bcm/yr figure is GTP throughput, not a pipeline rating).
validity.researcher_notes: LENGTH: GEM 106.5 km vs independent 'a 100-km pipeline' (OGJ) / '100km pipeline' (NS Energy). Not a material conflict — 100 km is an obvious round-number approximation and the more precise 106.5 km is geometrically plausible (Badra field ~33.04N,46.06E to Az-Zubaidiya PS ~32.77N,45.08E is ~95 km great-circle, so a routed 106.5 km is reasonable). But note 106.5 is sourced ONLY to the now-unverifiable OPC gateway page. DIAMETER: 18 in has NO independent corroboration; found in no accessible source (only the dead OPC page). CAPACITY: blank; not filled — no pipeline-specific throughput figure found (1.6 bcm/yr is the gas treatment plant capacity, not the line). DATE: commissioning 6 Dec 2017 is independently confirmed (OGJ) and would be a good add.

routes.start_name: Badra oil field gas treatment plant, Wasit province, Iraq (near Badra town, ~160 km SE of Baghdad, close to the Iranian border)
routes.end_name: Az-Zubaidiya (Al-Zubaidiya) power station, north of Al-Zubaidiya city, Wasit province, Iraq
routes.corridor_desc: Runs roughly WSW/SW across Wasit province, from the Badra field GTP in the far east of the province near the Iran border toward the Az-Zubaidiya thermal power station on the west bank of the Tigris north of Al-Zubaidiya city (south of Kut). Great-circle separation is ~95 km, consistent with the ~100 km (GEM 106.5 km) reported length. No published route trace was found, so the corridor is bounded only by the two endpoints and the intervening Wasit plain — medium confidence on the endpoints, low on the intermediate alignment (no sourced waypoints).
routes.researcher_notes: Endpoints established from independent sources: OGJ/NS Energy name both ends (Badra field GTP → Az-Zubaidiya power station) and the ~100 km length; offshore-technology anchors the Badra field in Wasit; power-technology profiles the Az-Zubaidiya (Zubaidiya) plant in Wasit. End coordinate 32.7736,45.0826 is the published Al-Zubaidiya power-station location (32°45'38.6"N 45°10'22.3"E). Start coordinate 33.04,46.06 is the Badra field/GTP area; the exact GTP pad within the field is not separately published, so treat start as field-centroid-level (~a few km uncertainty). No intermediate waypoint was sourced — none fabricated; the alignment across Wasit is inferred straight-corridor only. This is a route SUGGESTION for a later human routes-repo branch, not an applied route.

summary: P7471 confirmed (caveat): real, well-documented dry-gas trunk Badra field GTP → Az-Zubaidiya PS (~100 km, commissioned Dec 2017); not a duplicate of P4067 (different source field, same PS); caveats — both GEM citations are weak (OPC gov page now a JS gateway, FB post's 1065 km is the whole network not this line), diameter 18 in is unverified independently, length 106.5 vs sourced ~100 km, capacity legitimately blank.
